text.p: The average yield at the latest auction of three-month discount treasury bills slipped to 55.21 percent from 56.93 percent at the last sale on October 4, a Ukrainian central bank official said on Tuesday.
The results of Tuesday's auction, compared to the last issue of three-month T-bills, were as follows:
Amount sold 40.00 million UAH 16.33 million UAH
Actual amount raised 35.16 million UAH 14.30 million UAH
Ukraine's central bank sold 400,000 T-bills, the bank's statement said.
The date of the next auction of discount three-month T-bills is unfixed.
The average yield at the latest auction of six-month discount treasury bills slipped to 59.57 percent from 59.90 percent at the last sale on October 3, a central bank statement said.
The results of Tuesday's auction, compared to the last issue of six-month discount T-bills, were as follows:
Actual amount raised 6.73 million UAH 35,450 UAH
The central bank sold 87,385 T-bills, the bank's statement said.
The date of the next auction of six-month discount T-bills is unfixed.
The average yield at the latest auction of nine-month discount treasury bills rose to 61.48 percent from 56.21 percent at the last sale on August 21, a central bank statement said.
The results of Tuesday's auction, compared to the last issue of nine-month discount T-bills, were as follows:
Actual amount raised 3,420 UAH 2.50 trillion UAK
The central bank sold 50 T-bills, the bank's statement said.
The date of the next auction of nine-month discount T-bills is unfixed.
The average yield at the latest auction of 12-month discount treasury bills edged down to 62.75 percent against 62.93 percent at the last sale on October 3, a central bank statement said.
The results of Tuesday's auction, compared to the last issue of 12-month discount T-bills, were as follows:
The central bank sold 386 T-bills, the bank's statement said.
The date of the next auction of 12-month discount T-bills is unfixed.

On September 2, Ukraine introduced the hryvnia and removed the interim karbovanets currency from circulation on September 16, but some transactions are still recorded in the old currency. One hryvnia equals 100,000 karbovanets. --Kiev newsroom +380 44 229-2264
